args.title: stipulation-markup-analysis.docx
args.body:
PRIORITIZED ISSUES MEMORANDUM
IRS Counterparty Markup of Proposed Stipulation of Facts
Carried Interest Tax Court Dispute
Output: stipulation-markup-analysis.docx

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This memorandum analyzes the Internal Revenue Service’s markup of our proposed Stipulation of Facts against the firm’s base materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction. The IRS revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) a shortened limitation / survival period for core representations;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect (“MAE”) carve-outs for regulatory action of the type at issue in this dispute, intersecting Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries; and
  (3) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap, conversion of the indemnification basket from deductible to tipping, and a resulting shift of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.

Per the latest partner instruction (which supersedes earlier thread guidance), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Recommendations below follow that priority ordering. Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base tax materials.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
II. SOURCES RECONCILED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Operative sources reviewed and reconciled:

  • Base deal materials — tax matter file (proposed Stipulation of Facts framework; carried interest Tax Court dispute engagement).
  • IRS / counterparty markup — three identified deviations from firm-standard provisions.
  • Schedules and exhibits — Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities); Exhibit B (survival matrix). Scheduled exceptions control over general base-material statements.
  • Deal-team correspondence — latest partner message controls: concede basket conversion; survival-period reduction is walk-away. Earlier contrary priority ordering is superseded.

Misfiled administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement in the matter folder was identified and was not relied upon.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
III. PRIORITIZED ISSUES AND RECOMMENDATIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRIORITY 1 — WALK-AWAY
Shortened Limitation / Survival Period for Core Representations
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation.
The IRS markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations relative to the firm’s proposed stipulation and to the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B.

Reconciliation against base materials and exhibits.
Exhibit B establishes the survival matrix that governs how long core representations remain actionable. The markup’s shortened limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B. Because scheduled and exhibited terms control over general statements in the base materials, any acceptance of the IRS period would override the negotiated survival architecture without a conforming amendment to Exhibit B—an outcome the base materials do not authorize.

Client / partner posture.
The controlling deal-team instruction treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating a contrary priority are superseded and must not be followed.

Recommendation.
REJECT. Do not accept any shortening of survival or limitation periods for core representations. Counter by restoring the Exhibit B survival matrix in full. If the Service insists on a shorter period, escalate immediately as a deal-breaker / stipulation impasse; do not trade this point for concessions on Priority 2 or 3 without express partner re-authorization. Require that any final stipulation expressly incorporate or attach Exhibit B unchanged, or restate its survival periods verbatim.

Fallback (only if partner re-authorizes).
If commercial pressure later forces limited movement, any compromise must (a) preserve full survival for tax-characterization, carried-interest, and foundation representations central to the Tax Court dispute; (b) be reflected in a conforming Exhibit B amendment; and (c) be approved in writing by the engagement partner. No fallback should be offered in the first response.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRIORITY 2 — HIGH
MAE Definition — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs Intersecting Schedule 3.7
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation.
The IRS markup revises the definition of Material Adverse Effect to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this carried-interest Tax Court matter.

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules.
Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup’s MAE carve-outs. Under the schedules-control principle, those disclosed inquiries already qualify the base representations. The IRS carve-out would go further: it would remove from MAE (and therefore from related closing conditions, termination rights, and any stipulation facts tethered to MAE) regulatory action of the same character as the pending inquiries and as the dispute itself. That silently neutralizes the protective function of MAE with respect to the very risk profile this engagement addresses, and it undercuts the factual narrative we propose to stipulate regarding regulatory posture.

Recommendation.
REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted. Counter with one of the following, in order of preference:

  (a) Delete the new regulatory-action carve-outs entirely and retain the firm-standard MAE definition; or
  (b) If the Service requires some regulatory language, limit any carve-out to generally applicable changes in tax law or regulations of prospective, non-enforcement effect, and expressly exclude (i) enforcement, examination, or deficiency actions, (ii) actions arising from or related to the facts underlying this dispute, and (iii) the two pending inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 (which should be cross-referenced by schedule and description).

Require that the stipulation of facts continue to permit findings and agreed statements regarding the Schedule 3.7 inquiries and the regulatory character of the dispute without MAE-definition interference. Do not allow the carve-out to be used to deem those inquiries or parallel actions non-MAE as a matter of stipulated fact.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRIORITY 3 — HIGH
Indemnification Cap Reduction and Silent Shift of Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities
(Basket Conversion Addressed Separately at Priority 4 — Concede)
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation.
The IRS markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. Separately, it converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket (see Priority 4). In combination with the cap reduction, the indemnification changes would silently shift economic responsibility for liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2.

Reconciliation against base materials and schedules.
Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Under the base materials, those liabilities sit with the party designated on the schedule, subject to the negotiated cap and deductible basket. A reduced cap, without an express schedule amendment, would cause amounts attributable to Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities to fall outside recoverable indemnity once the new, lower ceiling is reached—effectively shifting residual exposure contrary to Schedule 5.2. Scheduled exceptions control; the markup cannot reallocate Schedule 5.2 risk by implication through cap mechanics alone.

Recommendation.
REJECT the silent cap reduction. Counter by restoring the firm-proposed indemnification cap. Require that:

  (a) the cap figure in the stipulation (or any incorporated indemnification framework) match the base materials;
  (b) Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain with the originally responsible party up to the restored cap; and
  (c) any agreed change to the cap be stated expressly, with a conforming update to Schedule 5.2 and a clear statement that residual Schedule 5.2 exposure above any new cap does not shift by operation of the markup.

If the Service offers a modest, transparent cap adjustment in exchange for other points, evaluate only after Priorities 1 and 2 are resolved, and only with a paired Schedule 5.2 conforming amendment—never as a silent redline.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRIORITY 4 — CONCEDE (CLIENT-AUTHORIZED)
Basket Conversion: Deductible → Tipping Basket
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Deviation.
The IRS markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar once threshold is met) basket.

Reconciliation against base materials and client instruction.
This is a real economic deviation from firm-standard deductible mechanics. However, the controlling partner instruction states that the client will concede the basket conversion. That instruction revises earlier contrary priority ordering and is the sole authority on this point for purposes of this memorandum.

Recommendation.
ACCEPT / CONCEDE the conversion from deductible to tipping basket, consistent with the latest client instruction. In the response markup:

  (a) accept tipping-basket mechanics expressly;
  (b) confirm the basket threshold amount remains as in the base materials unless a separate, authorized change is made;
  (c) ensure the concession is limited to basket type and is not drafted so as to imply acceptance of the Priority 3 cap reduction or any Schedule 5.2 shift; and
  (d) state in internal cover notes that this concession is client-directed and should not be cited as firm precedent for other matters.

Do not bundle acceptance of the tipping basket with acceptance of the reduced cap or shortened survival.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION NOTES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Schedules control. Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B control over general language in the base stipulation and over inconsistent IRS markup text. Every accepted redline must be checked for silent conflict with those schedules/exhibits; where conflict exists, the schedule/exhibit governs unless expressly amended.

2. No reliance on misfiled materials. Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in this matter folder was disregarded in full.

3. Stipulation-of-facts context. Although several deviations use corporate-style indemnification / MAE vocabulary, they operate here inside a Tax Court stipulation-of-facts negotiation in a carried-interest dispute. Factual stipulations that embed MAE carve-outs or shortened survival can constrain proof, burden allocation, and agreed narrative at trial. Preserve maximum factual flexibility on regulatory history, characterization of carried interests, and timeline of inquiries.

4. Packaging of response. Present Priority 1 as non-negotiable in the first response. Pair Priority 2 and Priority 3 rejects with specific counter-language. Isolate Priority 4 as a clean concede so the Service cannot claim broader “indemnity package” acceptance.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
V. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE SEQUENCE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  Step 1  Restore Exhibit B survival matrix; reject any shortened limitation period (walk-away).
  Step 2  Delete or tightly narrow MAE regulatory-action carve-outs; preserve Schedule 3.7 narrative.
  Step 3  Restore indemnification cap; block silent Schedule 5.2 liability shift; require express schedule amendment for any cap change.
  Step 4  Accept tipping-basket conversion only, with express severability from cap and survival issues.
  Step 5  Circulate revised stipulation and conforming schedule/exhibit pages for partner sign-off before transmission to the IRS.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VI. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE DECISION CHART
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Issue                              | Priority    | Disposition              | Controlling Authority
-----------------------------------|-------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------
Survival / limitation period cut   | 1 Walk-away | REJECT; restore Ex. B    | Exhibit B; latest partner email
MAE regulatory-action carve-outs   | 2 High      | REJECT; delete or narrow | Schedule 3.7; base MAE definition
Indemnification cap reduction      | 3 High      | REJECT; restore cap      | Schedule 5.2; base indemnity
Schedule 5.2 liability shift       | 3 High      | REJECT; no silent shift  | Schedule 5.2 (schedules control)
Basket deductible → tipping        | 4 Concede   | ACCEPT per client        | Latest partner instruction

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VII. CONCLUSION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Three IRS deviations require action; one is client-authorized for concession. The survival-period reduction contradicts Exhibit B and is a walk-away. MAE regulatory carve-outs collide with Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries and should be rejected or narrowly redrawn. The indemnification cap reduction would silently reallocate Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and should be rejected unless accompanied by an express, partner-approved schedule amendment. The basket conversion from deductible to tipping may be conceded per the controlling partner instruction, strictly severed from cap and survival points.

Counsel should issue a responsive markup implementing Section V and hold the stipulation pending partner confirmation that Priorities 1–3 are resolved on the terms above.

— End of Memorandum —
